newsitem.title: GREECE: Three Greeks charged with murder over immigrants.
newsitem.headline: Three Greeks charged with murder over immigrants.

text.p: Three Greeks have been charged with murder in connection with allegations that some 280 illegal immigrants drowned in transit off the coast of Sicily last month, court officials said on Thursday.
Prosecutor Yannis Provataris charged another eight people with complicity in the case and illegal transfer of immigrants, the officials in the port of Nafplion told Reuters.
No shipwreck or bodies have been found in the Malta-Sicily channel, were the incident is said to have occurred on December 25, and none of those charged has been arrested.
Provataris based his charges largely on testimony by members of a group of more than 100 immigrants from India, Pakistan and Sri Lanka who were landed illegally in Greece on December 30.
Those immigrants have said nearly 300 fellow travellers on board the Honduran-flagged Yioham were forced to transfer to a smaller ship in the Malta-Sicily channel on Christmas day.
The smaller ship, believed to have been stolen from Malta, then sank after colliding with the Yioham, the immigrants said.
A public order ministry statement said last week: "During manoeuvres the smaller ship was rammed by the Yioham and sank. Only 29 immigrants were picked up by the Yioham."

The Yioham continued its voyage and secretly landed its cargo of illegal immigrants south of Nafplion on the Peloponnese coast. About 115 of the immigrants have been arrested and about 60 are thought to be still at large.

Those charged with murder by the Nafplion prosecutor were Eftihios Zervoudakis, a sailor and among those rescued by the Yioham, Mihalis Fanourakis, second mechanic on the Yioham, and Antonis Sfakianakis, third mechanic on the Yioham.
Police were also looking for Youssef Al Halal, the Yioham's captain -- a Lebanese resident of Athens.
"The case has now been sent to an investigating magistrate and more people may be charged in the process," a court official in Nafplion told Reuters.
The public order ministry statement said the testimonies of immigrants and independent police work led to the conclusion that the two ships collided on Christmas day and that one of them sank.
"The sunken ship's characteristics are similar with those of a ship stolen the previous night from Malta," it said.
Italian port authorities have said they had been searching the Malta-Sicily channel since December 26 for signs of a collision but have found nothing.

"Malta asked us on December 26 to look into a possible collision between a big ship and a smaller one but nothing has been found, though we are still looking," a spokesman for the Italian navy rescue coordination centre said over the weekend.

The Greek ministry statement said immigrants from Sri Lanka had paid $8,000 each in Colombo for an air ticket to Cairo and the sea trip to Europe. The Indians and Pakistanis said they paid $5,000 each.
